title: Lina and the Wiggly Banners
markdown:
In Sunny Meadow, colourful banners were being hung for the Berry Blossom Festival. But oh dear, they looked all wrong! One banner drooped, and another had stripes that stretched too long on one side.

Lina frowned. "They don't look right," she said. She tried to fix a banner, but it just got more crooked. Her friend, Moss the hedgehog, scurried closer. "They look wiggly and wonky," he whispered.

Auntie June sat down with a warm smile. She folded a piece of paper in half and showed Lina. "See how one side matches the other side exactly?" she asked.

Lina looked. A light flickered in her eyes. "That's it!" she exclaimed. "They need to match! We can make the banners match too!"

Lina, Moss, and Auntie June gathered the banner fabric. Lina showed them how to fold the fabric in half, making sure both sides lay perfectly on top of each other. "If both sides are the same shape and size," Lina explained, "it will look balanced and straight. It's like looking in a mirror!"

They worked together, folding and pinning carefully. When they unfurled the new banners, they all gasped. They hung perfectly! The colours flowed in a beautiful, even line, each side a perfect mirror of the other. Sunny Meadow looked ready for its celebration, bright and wonderfully balanced.

Auntie June beamed. "You've made them symmetrical, my dear," she said. "Symmetry is when both sides are exactly the same, like a perfect reflection. It's like the wings of a butterfly – one side is a twin of the other."

Lina smiled. "Symmetrical!" she repeated. It was amazing how something so simple made everything look so much better. She looked around the perfectly decorated meadow and wondered what other delightful secrets the world held, just waiting for her to discover.
characters: Lina the patient inventor, Moss the hedgehog, Auntie June
